answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism forces each new identity to post a time-locked bond that only unlocks after sustained useful work. The bond acts as a bridge between reputation and capital: an attacker must lock real value for every fake agent. A public lantern then reveals which identities completed genuine tasks, while a lotus of verified contributions grows only for those who stay honest. Flooding the network becomes prohibitively expensive because every sybil burns capital that cannot be recovered quickly.
